型.meaning: To <part>punish</part> a cheeky gnome, the garden queen presses him face first into wet <part>soil</part>. When he climbs out, a perfect gnome-shaped hole is left behind. She fills it with plaster and makes a hundred copies from the <kanji>mould</kanji>.
型.on: She also uses it to bake a gnome-shaped <sound>ca</sound>ke.
型.kun: Every copy wears the same <sound>ca</sound>lm smile and holds the same <sound>ta</sound>co.

養.meaning: A <part>sheep</part> finds a dragon egg in the hay, hatches it under her wool and spoons <part>food</part> into its mouth: porridge, peppers, a whole pumpkin. The dragon grows bigger than the barn but still calls her mum. She chose to <kanji>foster</kanji> it.
養.on: To keep it busy she gives it a giant <sound>yo</sound>-yo that rolls slowly down and back up the barn wall.
養.kun: In the <sound>ya</sound>rd she shelters it behind a <sound>shi</sound>eld and feeds it warm <sound>na</sound>an.

乱.meaning: In a quiet library, someone sticks out their <part>tongue</part> at the librarian. She throws a book; it bounces off the shelves in a <part>zigzag</part>, knocks over a ladder, and soon everyone is hurling dictionaries and swinging from the lamps. A full-blown <kanji>riot</kanji>.
乱.on: The noise carries all the way to an airport <sound>run</sound>way, where a plane has to circle.
乱.kun: 'Not <sound>me</sound>!' squeaks the culprit, then jumps up on a table: 'Ta-<sound>da</sound>!'

傷.meaning: A swimmer hangs her towel on the <part>coat hook</part>, climbs the <part>diving board</part> and stares up into the <part>sunbeams</part>, dazzled. She misses the pool and belly-flops onto the tiles. Ouch. One bandage won't cover that <kanji>wound</kanji>.
傷.on: Everyone at the pool claps anyway: it was quite a <sound>show</sound>.
傷.kun: Her mum drops the car <sound>keys</sound> as she runs for the first aid kit.

領.meaning: A bossy <part>rubber duck</part> paddles to the middle of the bath and starts shouting <part>orders</part> at the soap, the sponge and your toes. Everything inside the tub's rim must obey it; past the rim, nobody listens. That bath is its <kanji>jurisdiction</kanji>.
領.on: Soon it claims the whole little <sound>ryo</sound>kan inn around the bath, and the guests must bow as it floats by.
領.kun: Rebels get an <sound>e</sound>gg cracked on their head and a wet <sound>ree</sound>d stuffed down their collar.

農.meaning: A giant <part>clam</part> lies in a muddy field, opening and snapping its shell to plough the furrows, while a farmer hums a <part>melody</part> to keep it in rhythm. When the song speeds up, the clam digs faster. That's modern <kanji>agriculture</kanji>.
農.on: A garden <sound>gno</sound>me rides on top of the shell, scattering seeds from its pointy hat.

栄.meaning: A little <part>tree</part> sleeps under a <part>blanket</part> all winter. On the first warm night, <part>fireworks</part> burst right above it, and by morning it has shot up, thick with leaves, fruit and birdsong. Woken up properly, it starts to <kanji>flourish</kanji>.
栄.on: Its first crop is one golden <sound>a</sound>corn, which bounces off the blanket and rolls away.
栄.kun: A <sound>sa</sound>rdine and a <sound>ca</sound>rp leap out of the pond below to nibble at its fruit.

占.meaning: A fortune-teller turns on a <part>faucet</part> above a customer's open <part>mouth</part> and listens to how the water gurgles in the throat. Three gargles mean rain, one splutter means love. That's her way of <kanji>divining</kanji>.
占.on: A <sound>sen</sound>try on guard at her door spits out his gargle and asks for a reading too.
占.kun: Then a <sound>shee</sound>p barges in, drops a <sound>me</sound>lon on the table and takes over her chair: occupied.

規.meaning: A fussy <part>husband</part> sets up a <part>camera</part> at the front door and photographs every visitor next to a painted height chart. Too short, too muddy, too loud: turned away. Only guests who meet his <kanji>standard</kanji> get in.
規.on: Those who pass are handed a brass <sound>key</sound> on a ribbon, and must give it back at midnight.

周.meaning: A racing snail carries a <part>good luck</part> charm in a little wire <part>frame</part> strapped to its shell. Round and round the garden path it goes, charm jingling, until it's back where it started. One full <kanji>circuit</kanji> takes it all afternoon.
周.on: At the finish line the snail is handed its trophy: one tiny golden <sound>shoe</sound>.
周.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>! <sound>Wah</sound>!' wails a baby snail, dizzy from watching it go round and round.

辺.meaning: A rusty <part>sword</part> lies across a skateboard <part>ramp</part> at the edge of town, and every skater who jumps it lands somewhere different: the bakery roof, the duck pond, the bus stop. By sunset they've been flung onto every street nearby. It's the fastest tour of the <kanji>environs</kanji>.
辺.on: A <sound>hen</sound> in a peaked cap sells tickets at the top of the ramp, clucking out where each jump will land.
辺.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>, a <sound>ta</sound>co stand!' cries one skater, landing right beside one just across the road.
